rules.statement: The exact-vector families are the comma-separated list of the spec sentence beginning "Exact vectors cover ", in order; the record binds that sentence's text, not the whole spec. Each family is declared once, in that order, with row selectors (an exact catalog id, or a prefix ending in ":*"), expanded against the current catalog at verification: every selector must match a row, never a closure row, and only layer:vector:* layer rows.
Further exact-vector domains are declared with their own spec anchor and row selectors.

Stored vector corpora are every tests/conformance/comparator-vectors/*/ directory (which must hold manifest.json), every crates/*/tests/fixtures/*-vectors.json file and every tools/*-vectors/ derivation directory. Each is declared exactly once with row selectors; its bytes, the vectors themselves, are bound by tree digest.

Every tests/oracle/*/ directory is declared exactly once: a vector oracle maps to the codec/profile rows its pinned reference values decide; an authority or profile input maps to no row. Oracle bytes are the evidence of those rows and are bound by their owners, not here.

rules.statement: The record binds the ids of the cases in tests/conformance/cases/registry.json. Each maps to the current case-label and layer:focused:* rows that name it as a candidate, and must be the case owner of at least one of them.

rules.spec_anchor: 3. Representative licensed or project-authored scene documents.
rules.statement: Checked by rule, never bound: tests/conformance/candidates/registry.json holds exactly one entry; it covers interaction:frames-text-assets, and each of its coverage rows is owned by the representative owner bound to that entry, which validates. Every other candidates/* directory is a superseded or unregistered collection, excluded by rule.

rules.spec_anchor: External scenes require consent or redistribution-compatible licensing and are
rules.statement: Every #84 case of tests/conformance/cases/representative/registry.json is checked here as tools/representative-intake/case.py checks it: its case.json is approved on a #85 comment binding its subject (case.py's subject computation), its retained-file inventory and intake manifest digest are current, the intake's sanitization retained_sha256 is the retained scene's digest, a license is present, and it has comparisons and at least one anchored crop besides whole. Unreferenced intake bundles and tests/public-scenes entries are excluded by rule.

Fuzz and property targets are crates/*/src/**/*_fuzz* (a module file or directory, outermost match), crates/*/tests/*_fuzz* and crates/*/tests/limits_* (a test binary with its module directory), and crates/*/{src,tests}/**/frame_batch_property. Each maps to exactly the row layer:adversarial:<name with - for _>. The record binds each target and the REQUIRED_RISKS it declares, not its source bytes.

Regression corpora are crates/*/tests/qualification/*-regressions.json. Each maps to exactly the row layer:regression:<name>, recording its digest, its case ids and public-facade case ids (each unique within its list) and its risks.

rules.statement: Each vector item maps to at least one owned row; every mapped layer row is owned; every owned mapped row's owner passes the ledger's checks (a case owner also passes its conformance verification). Registered cases, candidates, fuzz targets and regression corpora are owned as their rules state.
